Where it began

Peter Siddle was born in Traralgon, Victoria, on 25 November 1984, and grew up close by in Morwell, in Gippsland. Before cricket his sport was woodchopping, at a competitive level. He took up the game at 14 with the Latrobe Cricket Club and was soon making his mark: in one under-17 state match he took 11 for 47, a Victorian record.

After time at the Australian Cricket Academy he made his first-class debut for Victoria in November 2005, against the touring West Indians at the MCG.

The player

His Test debut came at Mohali in October 2008, and his first wicket was Sachin Tendulkar. He was named the ICC's Emerging Player of the Year in 2009, and that year he also helped Australia win the Champions Trophy. Between 2008 and 2019 he played 67 Tests and took 221 wickets at 30.67, with eight five-wicket hauls.

The day everyone remembers is 25 November 2010, his 26th birthday, in his first Test back after a long break, during the 2010–11 Ashes. He removed Alastair Cook and Matt Prior with successive balls, then trapped Stuart Broad leg before with a yorker to complete a hat-trick. He was the ninth Australian to take one in Tests and the first player ever to do it on his birthday. He finished with 6 for 54, his best Test figures.

What made him special

He was a workhorse in the best sense. Against South Africa at Adelaide in 2012 he sent down 63.5 overs in one Test, more than any other Australian fast bowler had bowled in a Test in the 21st century. He bowled to a tight line for long spells, and Kevin Pietersen found him especially hard to get away: Siddle dismissed him 10 times in Tests, more often than any other bowler managed. Across the back-to-back Ashes series of 2013 and 2013–14 he was the one Australian bowler to appear in every one of the ten Tests.

The bat was a lesser weapon, with a Test average of 14.73. Even so, on a tour of India he became the first number nine to make a fifty in both innings of a Test, which is not a bad claim for a tailender.

Away from the middle

International cricket ended for him in December 2019, but cricket itself never quite did. He played county cricket for Nottinghamshire, turned out for the Rest of the World in the bicentenary match at Lord's in 2014, and gave the Big Bash long service, notably with the Adelaide Strikers and, from 2024–25, the Melbourne Stars. In January 2026, aged 41, he bowled a ball at 145.8kph, and the next month he joined the Multan Sultans in the Pakistan Super League.

He became a vegan in 2012 and has done charity work for animal causes, among them the Penguin Foundation on Phillip Island.

And finally

His diet was known to include as many as 20 bananas a day. Whatever was in them, a fast bowler clocking 145.8kph at the age of 41 had clearly found something that worked.
